evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up GrimAge, the mortality clock that was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia in part 1 of this project (an effect explained by smoking). background_knowledge: Plasma TIMP-1 levels are reported to rise with age and in cardiovascular disease.

mechanism.rationale: The protein's biochemistry is well characterised. It is a secreted inhibitor of most MMPs and also acts as a growth factor via CD63 and ITGB1. Its dual roles, and the unclear causal direction in ageing, mean no clear inhibit or activate direction emerges.

evidence.value: Metalloproteinase inhibitor that functions by forming one to one complexes with target metalloproteinases, such as collagenases, and irreversibly inactivates them by binding to their catalytic zinc cofactor. Acts on MMP1, MMP2, MMP3, MMP7, MMP8, MMP9, MMP10, MMP11, MMP12, MMP13 and MMP16. Does not act on MMP14. Also functions as a growth factor that regulates cell differentiation, migration and cell death and activates cellular signaling cascades via CD63 and ITGB1. Plays a role in integrin signaling. Mediates erythropoiesis in vitro; but, unlike IL3, it is species-specific, stimulating the growth and differentiation of only human and murine erythroid progenitors

background_knowledge: TIMP1 is implicated in cancer progression, and MMP-inhibitor drugs have had musculoskeletal toxicity in the clinic.

arguments.summary: TIMP1 is a secreted MMP inhibitor and growth factor. About 21% of its papers mention ageing, and it is associated with several age-related diseases (COPD, coronary disease, Alzheimer disease), though association scores are low (about 0.1 or below). The project context concerns only its GrimAge methylation surrogate, which was not significantly different in the main meta-analysis model, so it says nothing about the measured protein. Tractability is limited to predicted antibody and PROTAC feasibility. There are no small-molecule leads and no clinical drugs, and the direction of modulation is unclear. I recommend deprioritise.
